definition.def: If you restrict something, you put a limit on it in order to reduce it or prevent it becoming too great.
examples: There is talk of restricting the number of students on campus. [VERB noun]
...restricting imports to 0.6 billion pounds of sugar per year. [VERB noun + to]

definition.def: To restrict the movement or actions of someone or something means to prevent them from moving or acting freely.
examples: Villagers say the fence would restrict public access to the hills. [VERB noun]
The government imprisoned dissidents, forbade travel, and restricted the press. [VERB noun]
These dams have restricted the flow of the river downstream. [VERB noun]

definition.def: If you restrict someone or their activities to one thing, they can only do, have, or deal with that thing. If you restrict them to one place, they cannot go anywhere else.
examples: Two knee injuries restricted him to only nine more league appearances. [VERB noun to noun]
The women were put on a diet that restricted them to 1,400 calories a day. [VERB noun to noun]
For the first two weeks patients are restricted to the grounds. [be VERB-ed + to]

definition.def: If you restrict something to a particular group, only that group can do it or have it. If you restrict something to a particular place, it is allowed only in that place.
examples: The hospital may restrict bookings to people living locally. [VERB noun + to]
Camping is restricted to five designated campgrounds. [VERB noun to noun]

examples.sentence: "It's the laws that restrict the supply of capital to the job market, not the advent of new technologies that causes unemployment."
In their active state, phytochrome molecules bind themselves to DNA to restrict plant growth.
We found that the mess was just too much, so we've decided to restrict this to the over 8s, as they are better able to clean up after themselves.
To restrict how much data can be mined from their computer use, and there are a few other ideas out there as well.
